preamble: There is no unconditioned sound change of /d/ to /p/. The only solid cases are total regressive assimilation in clusters: /d/ takes both the place and the voicelessness of a following /p/, giving a geminate /pp/. Latin shows it regularly in compounds with the prefix ad-, where the unassimilated spellings (adportō, adpetō) coexist with the assimilated ones (apportō, appetō).
phoneticEffects: Regressive Assimilation, Place Assimilation, Devoicing, Gemination

examples.note: Prefix-final /d/ assimilates totally to the following /p/.
